::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

:::{#sol-sum-rules}

Each step below applies @def-summation,
the distributive law (@thm-mult-distr),
or the commutative and associative laws of addition
(@thm-sum-symmetric and @thm-sum-assoc).

1.  Expand the sum, then factor out $c$:

    $$
    \ba
    \sumto{i}{3} c\, a_i
    &= c\, a_1 + c\, a_2 + c\, a_3
    && \text{(expand the sum)}
    \\ &= c \paren{a_1 + a_2 + a_3}
    && \text{(distributive law)}
    \\ &= c \sumto{i}{3} a_i
    && \text{(collect the sum)}
    \ea
    $$

2.  Expand the sum, then regroup the terms:

    $$
    \ba
    \sumto{i}{3} \paren{a_i + b_i}
    &= \paren{a_1 + b_1} + \paren{a_2 + b_2} + \paren{a_3 + b_3}
    && \text{(expand the sum)}
    \\ &= \paren{a_1 + a_2 + a_3} + \paren{b_1 + b_2 + b_3}
    && \text{(commutative and associative laws)}
    \\ &= \sumto{i}{3} a_i + \sumto{i}{3} b_i
    && \text{(collect the sum)}
    \ea
    $$

Neither argument uses the number of terms:
the same steps work for any lower and upper limits.

:::

:::
